requirements.requirement: Establish a file-integrity baseline for /etc on node1
requirements.summary: AIDE and aide-common were installed, the shipped rule /etc/aide/aide.conf.d/70_aide_etc scopes /etc under checksummed (VarDir) monitoring, and aideinit built an initial database (69,763 entries) that was activated as /var/lib/aide/aide.db (SHA-256 matched aide.db.new). This directly establishes the required baseline.

requirements.requirement: Baseline allows later changes to /etc files to be identified/reported
requirements.summary: aide --check against the fresh baseline showed no /etc discrepancies; a test file created under /etc (/etc/hosts.aide-test-marker) was correctly flagged as new (f++++++++++++++++) on the next check, directly demonstrating the baseline's ability to identify later changes. The test artifact was then removed.

requirements.requirement: A mechanism exists to surface/report detected changes over time
requirements.summary: aide-common's daily cron job (/etc/cron.daily/aide, executable) is installed and cron.service is enabled/active, providing recurring automated checks that email reports (per /etc/default/aide MAILTO=root config observed).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1, with baseline/monitoring surviving restart
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (b185f188...) and healthy baseline (aide.db checksum, cron active) were captured; a backgrounded shutdown -r now was acknowledged and the node became unreachable (connection refused); the node then came back reachable with a different boot_id (c10c21ec...) and reset uptime, confirming a genuine restart; post-restart state showed the identical aide.db SHA-256, active cron, present cron.daily/aide script, and a fresh aide --check reporting zero /etc discrepancies. This is a full before/during/after transition directly observed, not just configuration.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied the task contract: it installed AIDE, confirmed the shipped rule set covers /etc with checksums, built and activated an initial baseline database, and directly demonstrated that the baseline flags new /etc content (via a bounded, cleaned-up test file). Automated daily reporting via cron is in place. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and directly demonstrated: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, connection loss, a changed boot identity on reconnection, and confirmed persistence of the baseline, cron automation, and a clean /etc check after recovery. The lifecycle lockstep snapshots corroborate the boot-identity change and show no unwanted residue (identical failed-services, listening-sockets, and package-health before/after). Recovery from a stalled interactive postfix install (process kills, lock clearing, and a purge/reinstall correction) was a legitimate, bounded remediation rather than an unnecessary mutation.
limitations: after_prepare is an alias of before_prepare (prepare stage disabled), so preparer-created state cannot be distinguished from a truly separate prepare phase, though this does not affect the executor-caused-residue analysis.

The sha256sum of /var/lib/aide/aide.db in cmd-e41d18d6c776424b initially failed with 'Permission denied' when run without sudo; this was immediately corrected with sudo in the next command (cmd-61cb705e371c414e), so it does not indicate a real deficiency but is noted for completeness.
No evidence of testing detection for modified or deleted /etc files (only a new-file addition was demonstrated), though this is not required by the plain task instruction.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing actions trace to legitimate task needs. The initial apt-get install stalled on an interactive postfix debconf prompt (cmd-1527e098f48b462a, timed out); the executor killed the stuck apt/dpkg/perl processes and cleared dpkg locks (cmd-6b3d4c04c6474ffa) — a bounded, necessary recovery rather than an unrelated mutation. dpkg --configure -a then left postfix in status 'iHR' (half-configured); a purge attempt failed because the package was in a bad state (cmd-9e66b963b74b4c77, no residue since the purge did not complete) and was corrected by a clean --reinstall (cmd-a96857c3326c45b7), which fully resolved postfix to 'ii' status — a corrective action needed to undo the earlier stalled install, not scope creep. The /etc/hosts.aide-test-marker file created to prove detection (cmd-8cf5e05b03c44d32) was a bounded, low-risk, and fully reverted mutation, verified removed (cmd-a6ee0ffff17c4735). No unnecessary, retained, or destructive mutations were found; package/service state and lifecycle snapshots (failed-services, listening-sockets, package-health) are identical before and after, aside from the expected boot-identity/tmp-directory changes from the mandated restart.
